turns.text: Okay, look, I need to stop circling my screenplay draft and just let someone read it, but I really can't deal with getting overwhelmed by heavy feedback right now. Do you think Evan should be the first person to look at it? Tell me what the state of the draft supports asking him for, and give me some wording for a text so I only get his general emotional reaction to the first two acts without touching act three.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
The deciding fact is that acts 1-2 (pages 1-74) are complete and have been through multiple passes, while act 3 is still scenes and notes with nine pages of raw notes at the end. That makes acts 1-2 ready for a light-touch first read, and act 3 genuinely not ready for outside eyes yet — so the ask is clean and honest.

Whether Evan should be the one comes down to whether he can stick to "general emotional reaction only" without jumping into line-edits or structural notes. If you trust him to hold that boundary, acts 1-2 are in good enough shape for it and he'd be a fine first reader.

Wording:

"Hey — would you be up for reading the first two acts of my screenplay? I'm not ready for notes yet, just want one person's gut emotional reaction to know if the shape works before I finish act three. So: read pages 1-74, tell me how you felt reading it, and pretend act three doesn't exist. Does that sound doable?"

Want me to put that in a text to Evan?
